plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $3, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $3, ensuring I only win when profitable (paying less than $3) and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down - bidding above value risks winning at a loss, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit in this single-round game.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy, since the price paid is determined by the second-highest bid, not one's own bid. Bidding above value risks overpaying (winning at a price above value), while bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' strategies, the optimal action is to bid exactly my valuation of $11.
